identity_notes: This retrieval was heavily contaminated with three unrelated clusters that share only keyword/abbreviation overlap with 'methionine': (1) S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAMe), a distinct, separately marketed supplement/metabolite of methionine, which accounts for roughly 25 rejected records (antidepressant trials, liver-disease trials, a mania case report) -- these are flagged different_substance throughout since SAMe is not what an 'L-Methionine' supplement label delivers; (2) [11C]-methionine as an INJECTED PET radiotracer for brain-tumor imaging, an entirely different diagnostic use unrelated to oral supplementation; and (3) 'methionine' as a keyword inside paracetamol/acetaminophen literature (N-acetylcysteine/methionine antidote context), broiler-chicken/dairy-cow feed-science studies, and numerous MTHFR/homocysteine/one-carbon-metabolism OBSERVATIONAL biomarker studies that do not administer methionine as an intervention. After removing these, only 11 genuine oral L-methionine or D-methionine human trials/case reports remained. Most of these retrieved abstracts were truncated before the results sentence in this scope, leaving direction_primary 'unresolved' for the majority -- notably 25464565 (noise-induced hearing protection) and 15477550 (AIDS myelopathy) have real but uncaptured results that should be re-pulled in full before any efficacy claim. Two positive-appearing findings did survive in the captured excerpts: D-methionine reduced cisplatin-induced ototoxicity in a small (n=27 analyzed) Phase 2 trial (34622731), and methionine appeared to help arrest nitrous-oxide-induced myeloneuropathy in a 2-patient case series already on B12 (1403023). Several kept records combine methionine with other actives (antioxidant vitamins/minerals in 2103755, Hibiscus/Boswellia in 29974725) so methionine's isolated contribution cannot be determined from those records.
